name: Baruch
bio: Baruch son of Neriah was Jeremiah's scribe and loyal companion. Jeremiah entrusted him with the deed to the field bought from Hanameel, a sign of future restoration (Jeremiah 32:12-16). In the fourth year of Jehoiakim, Jeremiah dictated to Baruch a scroll containing all his prophecies; since Jeremiah himself was barred from the temple, Baruch read it aloud there on a fast day. When officials heard of it, they had Baruch read it to them privately, then warned him and Jeremiah to hide before informing the king, who burned the scroll and ordered both men's arrest, though the LORD hid them. Jeremiah then dictated the scroll's words to Baruch all over again, with more added besides (Jeremiah 36:1-32). Baruch stayed with Jeremiah through the fall of Jerusalem and the flight of the remaining Jews to Egypt, where Jeremiah addressed a further message to him about his fear and the LORD's protection amid the coming disaster (Jeremiah 45:1-5). His brother Seraiah also served Zedekiah (Jeremiah 51:59).
